summary: Clearwater County 40-foot pole lookout built 1934 with an L-4 cab, rebuilt in 1953 per a timber association report and destroyed in 1972; no source describes the site now.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1972. No source describes what, if anything, remains at the site.

events.note: Archives West aerial photograph dated 1936, captioned Beohls Butte Lookout
Timber association annual report says the tower was completely rebuilt that year

evidence.supports: 1934 build as pole tower with L-4 cab
drive-up tag on the site listing
1953 rebuild per Potlatch Timber Protective Association annual report
evidence.quote: Boehls Butte Lookout tower was completely rebuilt this year.

evidence.supports: Potlatch Timber Protective Association named as the agency column

evidence.quote: 1953: Boehls Butte Lookout tower was completely rebuilt this year. (Potlatch Timber Protective Association Annual Report)

evidence.supports: photo caption Beohls Butte Lookout, Clearwater River
evidence.quote: Beohls Butte Lookout. Breakfast Creek. North Fork, Clearwater River (CTPA). Oblique aerial view.

corrections.why: Both sites describe a 40-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab, so the kind is a tower rather than unknown

notes_for_editor: Location conflict left unresolved: the record's point (46.86827, -115.87455) comes from firelookout.com, while the FFLA list gives 46.59890, -115.79500 for the same name in Clearwater; no correction made. The protective association is abbreviated CPTPA on firelookout.com and CTPA on the Idaho Fire Lookouts page and in the Archives West caption; the Forest Lookouts table names the Potlatch Timber Protective Association. The story uses the name from the 1953 report quoted there. The 1953 rebuild appears only on the Forest Lookouts page. The record's county is null; the sources give Clearwater County. No staffing source found in two searches.
